title: P104: attain and bound the final fixed six-stage reporting tick
body:
## Result and scope
The fixed #8035 word and its six-stage selector attain κ = 0.003890115286594445 under five inherited P104 premises on an ideal finite tape, a lower-endpoint improvement of 3.745×10⁻¹⁵. A strict upper of 0.003890115286594445189476955228 excludes the next 10⁻¹⁸ tick. We also prove the lowest usable finite tensor power and its second-order growth near the raw crossing. The target 0.00389046 remains open.

The 430-factor profile prices all 36 binary and 48 numerical calls with 31 and 10 debit bits, respectively. Its binary price is 1175715202810401744919/2⁷⁸, stopping gap 10⁻²¹. All 54 strict and four functional signed conditions pass. All-column action, owned erasure and restoration, compiler transfer, precision and tape accounting, and analytic recovery remain inherited.

## Provenance and validation
Canonical main e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57; #8035 ea776471bf8ed143a0625cf2d7532f65d15eb5f9; #8030 6285dd829114705862e8d91facaedc1f31d3cfcb. Parallel #8042 uses retimed transport. The #7257 shared CI repair is parent 0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026. Package tree e64dc92eea33914dd9b68e5e20df65647e406973.

Run `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-six-stage-resolution`. Eight registered cases passed in 768.16 s. After adding tape and dispatcher controls, the revised price case passed in 20.82 s and on cold export in 21.33 s; the other seven paths were unchanged. Two outward methods check the price. The feasible signed product gives −345550037539 with 138 physical shuttles and a small local H kernel. The production forwarding probe is separate; the astronomical production tape has no physical run.

## Attribution and next question
Ali Romman supplied the native words and compilers, DreamingOfClouds the #7852 toolkit, and Clear1nsight coordinated the work with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Passing the raw ceiling requires a changed paid or productive inventory, or a new funding theorem.
